newsitem.title: CHINA: Yuan ends down against US dollar in Shanghai.
newsitem.headline: Yuan ends down against US dollar in Shanghai.

text.p: The Chinese yuan closed down at 8.2907 on Thursday from Wednesday's 8.2900 against the U.S. dollar in Shanghai on a technical correction after two days of rises, dealers said.
The weighted average price on Wednesday was 8.2907.

The yuan opened slightly down at 8.2903 and hit an intraday high of 8.2900 early in the trading. It then fell to move in the range of 8.2906 and 8.2910 for most of the session, touching a sudden low of 8.2942.
Trading was active with most done at 8.2908, dealers said.
"The yuan continued its uptrend yesterday to touch the 8.2900 level again early in trading, but its upward trend was capped by selling pressure at that level," one dealer said.
"No intervention from the central bank was seen today," he said.
But the yuan remained at the higher level backed by active buying below the 8.2910 level, a second dealer said.
"Comments from the central bank offical help to strengthen the pro-yuan sentiment," he said.
Dai Xianglong, the head of the People's Bank of China, the central bank, was reported on Thursday as having said recently that tight money policy would be continued through the second half of 1997.
Dealers said demand for the yuan in the market should remain strong, supporting the local currency in the long term.
They said they expected the yuan to move around the 8.2910 level on Friday.
The yuan closed down slightly at an intraday low of 7.1800 from 7.1701 against 100 Japanese yen and lower at a low of 1.0705 from 1.0698 against the Hong Kong dollar.
